cites.quote: API tests use Vitest and Supertest against a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 with a fixed clock.
Every PRD requirement has at least one test whose name starts with its ID (DOC-1, APT-4, ...).
Without either, database tests are skipped.
The verifier skips coverage (the project has no coverage script), so no run reports coverage.
The route is added to the existing `specializationsRouter`.
Name ties compare ignoring case, with `doctor id as the final tie-break`.

rubric_items.reason: Prior F-1 is fixed. New tests read /api/doctors/1/slots for an empty date, a cancelled-only date and a booked date (test L145-169), which covers S-6 AC1-AC3. S-1 to S-5 and S-6 AC4 were already covered, so every changed path and every AC now has a test.

Assertions check observable results: exact toEqual on entries, exact key sets, ordered names and ids, slot counts and states. Prior F-2 is fixed by the 'Invented note' check (L95), and prior F-3 by the BAD_REQUEST error-code check (L136).

Covers 404 NOT_FOUND, 400 BAD_REQUEST for a malformed id, 400 'specialization is Inactive', the today+6 and today+7 boundaries, UTC midnight, started slots, booked and Cancelled slots, ties with and without a slot, an empty list and 21 unpaged doctors.

Uses Vitest and Supertest in api/test with an injected fixed clock. Each suite gets a fresh database behind skipIf(!pgAvailable()). Titles start 'HMS-11 REQ-n' like the neighbouring HMS-9 tests, and the fixture data is invented.

Gives no pass or coverage numbers and leaves them to the verifier. The stated count of 20 tests in three suites matches the file (18+1+1). checks.json shows test pass and coverage skip (exit 78). Only the test file changed (269 lines added, 0 deleted).
